translation: Pallavi: On the earth where the rain has fallen drop by drop, a wondrous fragrance; is it the scent of jasmine or not? It is the fragrance of the daughter of the soil, the fragrance of this daughter of the soil; on the earth where the rain has fallen drop by drop, a wondrous fragrance; is it the scent of jasmine or not? It is the fragrance of the daughter of the soil, the fragrance of this daughter of the soil

Verse 1: The fragrance she spreads, with grass flowers tucked all through her hair; the fragrance she spreads, with grass flowers tucked all through her hair; the fragrance of living creatures coming into season as the year begins; the fragrance of living creatures coming into season as the year begins; when winged termites swarm out of the anthill, a fragrance like a drop of ghee; when winged termites swarm out of the anthill, a fragrance like a drop of ghee; as the red rudra bugs creep over Mother Earth's breast, as the babbling of water and a million bees sing out like sa-ri-ga-ma; on the earth where the rain has fallen drop by drop, a wondrous fragrance; is it the scent of jasmine or not? It is the fragrance of the daughter of the soil, the fragrance of this daughter of the soil

Verse 2: The rain shower joined earth and sky as mother and child; the rain shower joined earth and sky as mother and child; life sprouted forth in the sleeping seed; life sprouted forth in the sleeping seed; in the lap of the earth where the clouds poured down, oh, the lush green children; in the lap of the earth where the clouds poured down, oh, the lush green children; but that land has no moisture, only the weeping in these farmers' eyes, in the cracks of the parched fallow fields, in the streams of the poor people's sweat; on the earth where the rain has fallen drop by drop, a wondrous fragrance; is it the scent of jasmine or not? It is the fragrance of the daughter of the soil, the fragrance of this daughter of the soil

Verse 3: How did the paddy crops vanish and these cotton crops come in like knives? How did the paddy crops vanish and these cotton crops come in like knives? Whose eyes grew envious of the sturdy plumpness of the maize? Whose eyes grew envious of the sturdy plumpness of the maize? Were the seeds we used to save for ourselves cheated away from us? Were the seeds we used to save for ourselves cheated away from us? Go to buy, and it burns like a firebrand; go to sell, and it's worth no more than the forest; did the multinational companies grow fat and send us up to the sacrificial altar? On the earth where the rain has fallen drop by drop, a wondrous fragrance; is it the scent of jasmine or not? It is the fragrance of the daughter of the soil, the fragrance of this daughter of the soil

Verse 4: Dung and leaves, the natural manures, have they vanished without a trace? Dung and leaves, the natural manures, have they vanished without a trace? The earthworms that turn the soil into manure, have they died inside the soil? The earthworms that turn the soil into manure, have they died inside the soil? Have poisoned crops come up, with leaves not even a goat will touch? Have poisoned crops come up, with leaves not even a goat will touch? Is the poison hidden in the seed itself? Is the pest born even before the leaf? Has that very pesticide become the farmers' curd and rice? On the earth where the rain has fallen drop by drop, a wondrous fragrance; is it the scent of jasmine or not? It is the fragrance of the daughter of the soil, the fragrance of this daughter of the soil

Verse 5: With no cooperative bank coming to help, have the debts piled up in heaps? With no cooperative bank coming to help, have the debts piled up in heaps? With not a raindrop in sight, has the crop failed to come to hand? With not a raindrop in sight, has the crop failed to come to hand? Even after sinking borewells, have the farmers' lives ended in graves? Even after sinking borewells, have the farmers' lives ended in graves? A famine of fodder for the cattle, oh, a time when no milk is to be had, oh; the dried-up acacia tree has become a gallows-swing for you; on the earth where the rain has fallen drop by drop, a wondrous fragrance, the smell of Mother Earth's lives burning, that acrid, scorching smell; on the earth where the rain has fallen drop by drop, a wondrous fragrance, the smell of Mother Earth's lives burning, that acrid, scorching smell

Verse 6: O grieving labourer, O farmer, don't turn to the noose; O grieving labourer, O farmer, don't turn to the noose; seeing your burnt-out life, don't just spread sorrow; seeing your burnt-out life, don't just spread sorrow; there is grain in the godowns, go on a famine march; there is grain in the godowns, go on a famine march; don't repay any debts, don't weep before those who come demanding; the government that looted your hard toil is the one in debt to you; on the earth where the rain has fallen drop by drop, a wondrous fragrance, the smell of Mother Earth's lives burning, that acrid, scorching smell

Verse 7: Cup your hands and catch the water that falls drop by drop; cup your hands and catch the water that falls drop by drop; breathe in to your heart's content the nectar of the soil's fragrance; breathe in to your heart's content the nectar of the soil's fragrance; let tanks and ponds become dams, save the water; let tanks and ponds become dams, save the water; turn the water of the downpours toward the drought-stricken land; come on, for the reforms that have become nooses, we must twist nooses of our own; for the reforms that have become nooses, we must twist nooses of our own; for the reforms that have become nooses, we must twist nooses of our own; for the reforms that have become nooses, we must twist nooses of our own; for the reforms that have become nooses, we must twist nooses of our own
summaryEn: Sinuku Sinuku ('Drop by Drop') is sung by Vimalakka on the album Vimalakka Hits (2023). It begins as a nature song and turns into a sharp protest about the farm crisis. The chorus celebrates the smell of earth after the first rain - not jasmine, but 'the fragrance of the daughter of the soil'. The first verses paint the monsoon's arrival through village detail: grass flowers, winged termites swarming from anthills, red rudra bugs, bees and running water, sleeping seeds sprouting as rain joins earth and sky 'as mother and child'. The mood darkens as the singer asks a chain of pointed questions. Why has paddy given way to cotton that cuts 'like knives'? Who cheated farmers of the seeds they used to save? Why have dung manure and earthworms disappeared, leaving poisoned crops and pesticide that becomes the farmers' 'curd and rice'? Debts, failed borewells and drought end in suicide, with a dried acacia tree becoming a gallows. The fragrance of rain turns into the smell of Mother Earth's lives burning. The last verses speak directly to farmers: do not take your lives, march for the grain in the godowns, save rainwater in tanks and ponds, and resist the economic 'reforms' that have become nooses.
summaryTe: ‘చినుకు చినుకు’ విమలక్క 2023 ‘విమలక్క హిట్స్’ ఆల్బమ్‌లో పాడిన పాట. ఇది ప్రకృతి గీతంగా మొదలై వ్యవసాయ సంక్షోభంపై పదునైన నిరసన గీతంగా మారుతుంది. తొలకరి చినుకు పడ్డ నేల వాసన మల్లెల గంధం కాదని, అది ‘మట్టి పిల్ల వాసన’ అని పల్లవి మురిసిపోతుంది. మొదటి చరణాలు వానాకాలం రాకను పల్లె దృశ్యాలతో చిత్రిస్తాయి - గడ్డి పూలు, పుట్టల నుండి ఊరే ఊసిళ్ళు, ఎర్రని రుద్ర పురుగులు, తుమ్మెదల ఝుంకారం, నీటి గలగలలు, మన్నును మిన్నును తల్లీబిడ్డలుగా కలిపిన వానజల్లుకు మొలకెత్తే విత్తనాలు. ఆ తర్వాత పాట గొంతు మారి ప్రశ్నల వర్షం కురిపిస్తుంది: వరి పోయి కత్తుల్లాంటి పత్తి ఎలా వచ్చింది? దాచుకునే మన విత్తనాలకు మోసం ఎవరు చేశారు? పెండ ఎరువులు, ఎర్రలు ఎందుకు మాయమయ్యాయి? పురుగుల మందే రైతుకు పెరుగన్నం ఎలా అయింది? అప్పులు, ఎండిన బోర్లు, కరువు రైతును ఉరికొయ్యకు నెడతాయి; ఎండిన తుమ్మచెట్టే ఉరి ఉయ్యాల అవుతుంది. వాన వాసన భూతల్లి బతుకులు కాలుతున్న కమురు వాసనగా మారుతుంది. చివరి చరణాలు రైతుకు నేరుగా చెబుతాయి: ఉరి వద్దు, గోదాముల్లోని ధాన్యం కోసం కరువు యాత్ర చేయి, చెరువులు కుంటల్లో నీటిని కాపాడు, ఉరితాళ్ళయిన సంస్కరణలకే ఉరితాళ్ళు పేనాలి.
